gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured figure: OutdoorGearLab's bench puts four under-$500 1 kWh stations within 30 Wh of each other on usable AC output (880–910 Wh), while its measured recharge time (about 0.8 h Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 vs about 1.8–2 h BLUETTI Elite 100 V2), its measured weight (25 lb vs 31.5 lb DJI) and The Solar Lab's idle draw (13.8 W Anker vs 18 W DJI) do separate them.
standout_why: I opened the one cited page (PopSci Black Friday deals, 2026-11-26) and two uncited results (willitrunpower.com under-$500 guide, outagepowerguide.com under-$500 review). PopSci gives only maker claims such as the '49-minute AC charge time'. Willitrunpower says 'We did not test these stations ourselves' and uses an assumed 0.85 factor. Outagepowerguide claims '5 Products Tested' but shows no test result. None gives a measured Wh, idle draw, measured recharge time or measured weight. I did not open the other deal trackers in the result list (powersized, gearranking, juicebench, batteryplaces, wattpowerstation, preparedstates, gagadget, dealschecked), so one of them could carry part of this.
decides: It does not overturn the pick; it removes capacity as a tiebreaker and sharpens the order. Measured usable energy is a tie (Jackery 910, Anker 890, BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 890, DJI 880 Wh, all GearLab), so the ranking rests on output watts, price, recharge time, weight and idle draw. On the measured figures the Anker C1000 Gen 2 is the lightest fast charger (25.2 lb, about 0.8 h, 13.8 W idle), and the DJI Power 1000 V2 is 6.3 lb heavier with the highest idle draw (18 W), which matters for a fridge left on the inverter all day. Our BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 matches the Anker on usable Wh and weight but took about 2 h to recharge in GearLab's test and 1 h 36–39 min in The Solar Lab's, against BLUETTI's '80% in 45 min' TurboBoost claim. That supports placing it third behind DJI and Anker, not above them. The BLUETTI AC180 delivered the most measured energy of any candidate (950 Wh) but at 36 lb. The Elite 100 mini has the lowest idle draw (about 13.5 W) and ran above 1,000 W in The Solar Lab's test despite its 700 W rating, which supports it as the light-loads pick.
